description: Baseline: monochrome code editor with gutter, text area, minimal status bar. No syntax highlighting, no current-line highlight, no header bar. Looks like nano.
ANSI syntax highlighting (TS/JS/Python/Bash via syntax-highlight.ts), header breadcrumb bar, active gutter line, rich status bar (language, encoding, indent, lines, scroll%). 4.4 to 8.0 in one shot.
Toolbar buttons (Save/Find/Goto) with accent colour and hover effects, current-line background highlight on gutter and text. Layout at 9, coherence at 9.
Relative line numbers (vim hybrid), ANSI-styled header breadcrumb (dim path, bright filename, accent icon), ANSI status bar (accent cursor pos, muted metadata). All 5 axes at 9.
Welcome screen for empty editor: branded WibWob Code Editor box, Quick Start shortcuts, Navigation reference. Fixes the empty void. Character to 10.
Indent guides (dim │ at 2-space boundaries in leading whitespace). Feature works but too subtle to see in tmux screenshot. No visual score change.

VSCode-style file tree sidebar (EXPLORER with file icons, current file highlighted, Ctrl+B toggle), 4 toolbar buttons. Complete IDE layout: sidebar + gutter + editor + header + status. Layout and coherence at 10.
Visual scroll position bar in status bar (█░░░░), pipe-separated status segments (lang│UTF-8│indent│lines│scroll). Aesthetic to 10. Four axes at 10.
Line counts in sidebar file tree (479, 927, 21). Adds info density but doesn't change overall visual score. Keeping as functionally useful.

Wiretext baseline: tool sidebar (Select/Box/Text/Line/Arrow/Pencil/Eraser), box style selector (4 styles), canvas with grid dots, header+status bars, keyboard shortcuts, undo/redo, export. Structure solid but grid dots render as tildes, box previews garbled.
